insurer: Niva Bupa Health Insurance Company Limited
sumInsured: Not specified (Base Sum Insured + Booster+ + Safeguard/Safeguard+ + ReAssure+/ReAssureX as per Policy Schedule/Variant)

great.name: Room Rent
great.quote: “We don’t limit your choice. Choose the room you like, but choose judiciously to protect your Sum Insured.”
great.explanation: No room rent cap is mentioned, so you can choose any room category during hospitalization. This helps avoid room-rent linked deductions that can reduce claim payouts in capped plans.

great.name: Built-in SI Buffer
great.quote: “Enjoy unlimited Sum Insured. The first paid claim in the life of the policy triggers ReAssure “Forever”. Once Triggered it stays for life, provided that the policy is renewed without break.”
great.explanation: After the first paid claim, ReAssure “Forever” gets triggered and continues for life as long as you renew without a break. This can provide additional coverage beyond the base Sum Insured in future claims.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: “...excluded until the expiry of 12months/24 months/ 36 months (as per Variant selected) of continuous coverage...”
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are not covered for 12/24/36 months depending on the variant selected. A shorter PED wait means earlier coverage for conditions you already have.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: “...excluded until the expiry of 24 months/12 months (as per Variant Selected) of continuous coverage...”
good.reference: Section 5.1.2 Specified disease/procedure waiting period (Code- Excl02)
good.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are not covered for 12 or 24 months depending on the variant selected. This matters because claims for listed procedures can be rejected until the waiting period ends.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: “Expenses related to the treatment of any Illness within 30 days from the first Policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an Accident...”
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are excluded for the first 30 days from policy start, while accidents are covered immediately. This is a standard market waiting period you should plan around when buying a new policy.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: ...for 60 days before the date of admission...
good.reference: Section 4.1.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for up to 60 days before the date of admission, if linked to a covered hospitalization. This reduces out-of-pocket costs for tests and consultations leading up to admission.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.reference: Section 4.1.3 Expenses before and after hospitalization (Pre & Post hospitalization)
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered for up to 180 days after discharge, if linked to the covered hospitalization. This helps pay for follow-up medicines, diagnostics, and consultations after you leave the hospital.

good.name: Modern Treatments
good.quote: “We pay for Modern treatments, up to Base Sum Insured for the list as specified below:”
good.explanation: Modern treatments are covered up to the Base Sum Insured for the listed procedures. This is useful for newer medical technologies, but coverage is limited to the specified list.

good.name: Domiciliary Hospitalization
good.quote: “Home Care Treatment means treatment availed by the insured person at home which in normal course would require care and treatment at a hospital but is actually taken at home provided that...”
good.explanation: Home care/domiciliary treatment is covered when the treatment would normally require hospitalization but is taken at home subject to conditions. This can help when hospital admission is not possible or advisable.

good.name: Cashless Network
good.quote: “Cashless claim facility is available at our network hospitals ONLY. As list of network hospitals is dynamic, for the latest list, refer to our website www.nivabupa.com.”
good.explanation: Cashless treatment is available only at the insurer’s network hospitals, and the list is maintained on the website. This matters because going to a non-network hospital usually means reimbursement instead of cashless.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: “The expenses that are not covered or subsumed into room charges / procedure charges / costs of treatment are placed as Annexure I.”
bad.explanation: Consumables/non-payable items are handled as per Annexure I, meaning many such items may be excluded or only indirectly covered if bundled into other charges. This can lead to significant out-of-pocket expenses during hospitalization.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: “4.1.16. Co-Payment: It is the percentage of admissible claim amount You would have to bear for every claim, Rest we will pay.”
bad.explanation: A co-payment is described as a percentage of every admissible claim amount that you must bear. This is a negative because any applied co-pay increases your out-of-pocket share on each claim.

unclear.name: No Claim Bonus
unclear.quote: “Cumulative Bonus means any increase or addition in the Sum Insured granted by the insurer without an associated increase in premium.”
unclear.reference: Definition 2.1.8 (definition only; no benefit statement found)
unclear.explanation: Only the definition of Cumulative Bonus is provided, but the wording here does not confirm whether any no-claim bonus is actually offered. If no NCB is provided in the benefits/schedule, you won’t build extra Sum Insured for claim-free years.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
